channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Monochromatic Awards 2026 · Dodho Magazine
item.description: Fifth edition of the Dodho Monochromatic Awards, celebrating monochromatic photography in all interpretations — traditional black and white, grayscale, sepia, cyanotype, or any single-tone variation. Jury looks for clear vision, defined intention, and strong execution. Winners and finalists are featured in the Monochromatic Awards 2026 annual printed book (30×30 cm, premium matte paper). The top winner receives 'Photographer of the Year' recognition. Three category prizes plus two honorable mentions receive certificates and editorial visibility. Open globally, individuals or collectives. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: €30 (3) / €45 (6) / €60 (12). Prize: Photographer of the Year + annual book inclusion.

item.title: Passage Art-Residency-Programme 2026 · Polygona Kunstverein / KOBRA
item.description: Four-week artist-in-residence programme in the Wittenberg region of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, dedicated to photography and film. Two themed residencies for October 2026: Topic 1 at Ferropolis (the historic Zschornewitz coal-fired power station — energy production, post-industrial landscapes); Topic 2 at the Reformationsgeschichtliche Forschungsbibliothek Wittenberg (a Reformation-era research library — knowledge, visual representation). €5,000 grant per residency, plus €1,000 supplement for artists with children. On-site accommodation, research support, and curatorial guidance provided. Open to national and international artists aged 18+; students not eligible. Notification of results from 20 June 2026. — Deadline: May 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 grant + accommodation.

item.title: CCI + WOPHA Fellowship 2026 · Pérez Art Museum Miami
item.description: Joint fellowship from PAMM's Caribbean Cultural Institute (CCI) and Women Photographers International Archive (WOPHA), for emerging and mid-career women and non-binary photographers from the Caribbean and its diaspora. Hybrid program runs September–November 2026, with an in-person residency at El Espacio 23 in Miami during September. Fellow receives a stipend, production funds up to $4,000, and round-trip airfare to Miami if not currently based there. Photographic practice broadly defined to include cameraless, computational, and augmented processes, as well as image archiving and circulation. Includes mentorship, curatorial resources, and engagement with the academic community at FIU-LACC. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Stipend + $4,000 production.

item.title: Camille Lepage Award 2026
item.description: Annual €8,000 award supporting a photojournalist committed to a long-term reporting project. Established by the family of Camille Lepage, the photojournalist killed while reporting in the Central African Republic in 2014. Funded for the tenth year by the SAIF (Société des Auteurs des Arts Visuels et de l'Image Fixe). The award helps a photographer carry out and complete a reporting project already under way. Open to professional photojournalists with no restriction on age, gender, or nationality. Award presented in September 2026 at the International Festival of Photojournalism Visa pour l'Image-Perpignan. The winning report must be completed within one year so that it can be presented at the 2027 festival as an exhibition or evening show. — Deadline: May 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €8,000.

item.title: CIAR Fall Artists' Residency 2026 · Cuttyhunk Island Artists' Residency
item.description: Eight-day residency on Cuttyhunk Island off the Massachusetts coast, September 9–16, 2026. Open to visual artists at all career stages working across drawing, painting, collage, small sculpture, photography, and video. Artists must have a portable studio practice suitable for the island setting. Programming includes communal meals prepared by resident chefs, complimentary golf carts to roam the island, and conversations with visiting artists Claudia Keep and Randall Exon. Housing at the historic Avalon Inn (linens and towels provided); base cost $1,950 (triple) to $3,600 (single) plus ferry travel. Multiple full and partial fellowships available — the new Environmental Artist Fellowship, the Open Merit Fellowship, the Paul Cuffe Fellowship for an artist of color, the Wellspring Fellowship for parent artists, and work-study options — covering up to the full residency cost. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: 8-day island residency.

item.title: Urban 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of urban environments. Open to street photography that captures the people inhabiting these spaces, cityscapes, architecture, and beyond. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (4–30 September 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit 1–8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email. — Deadline: May 22, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Pink 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition exploring the colour pink across any genre — nature, urban settings, portraits, still life, or beyond. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (4–30 September 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit 1–8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email. — Deadline: May 22, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: PhotoArtDoc 2026 Open Call — State of Transition
item.description: Annual photography competition from PhotoArtDoc, a festival at the intersection of documentary and art organised by the Belarusian Independent Photographic Association (founded 2023). Theme: TRANSFORMATION — State of Transition, exploring how individuals navigate continuous change and uncertainty as a fundamental condition. Open to photographers and artists working with photography worldwide. Image transformation techniques such as montage, collage, and multiple exposure are permitted; methods must be described. 1st place wins exhibition in Vilnius, Lithuania, plus zine publication and online gallery feature. 2nd and 3rd places featured in the PhotoArtDoc 2026 zine and online gallery. Projects must have been created or completed between 2024 and 2026; maximum two projects per author. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition in Vilnius + zine publication.

item.title: Photometria Awards 2026 — Coming of Age · Photometria International Photography Festival
item.description: Open call for the 18th Photometria International Photography Festival in Ioannina, Greece. Theme: Coming of Age (18+) — exploring the layered and evolving condition of growing up, moments of rupture, and the tension between freedom and responsibility. Sole judge: Alec Soth (Magnum, Guggenheim Fellow). 1st prize: Nikon Z30 Kit with NIKKOR Z DX 12-28mm lens. 2nd and 3rd: signed photo album by Alec Soth. One top-three winner receives a solo exhibition at the next festival. Top 25 photos exhibited in Ioannina during the 18th edition (Sep–Nov 2026) and travel to other cities in Greece. AI-generated images not accepted. Entry: free for 1 photo, €5 for 3 photos. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: Free / €5. Prize: Nikon Z30 + solo exhibition.

item.title: Solo Exhibition June 2026 · All About Photo
item.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (June 1–30, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images. — Deadline: May 19, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Watershed
item.description: Themed juried exhibition exploring water as subject, symbol, tool, and essential aspect of life. Juried by Luther Smith, photographic artist and Emeritus Professor of Art Photography at Texas Christian University, with work in the Amon Carter Museum, Library of Congress, Dallas Museum of Art, and other major institutions. Exhibition at Pool Gallery, Fort Worth, July 3–25, 2026, with closing reception July 25. $400 first place, $250 second, $150 third, plus up to 5 honorable mentions. Open internationally to all skill levels. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: $30–$40 / 5 images. Prize: $400 first, $250 second, $150 third.

item.title: Vicinity 2026: What's Going On? · Perspective Gallery
item.description: 9th Annual Juried Exhibition. Inspired by Marvin Gaye's 1971 album exploring social conflict, the show invites artists to respond to 'What's going on?' through inner landscapes or broader human conditions — social, cultural, environmental. Juried by Jan Tichy, professor at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago in Photography and Art & Technology/Sound Practices, with work in MoMA and Israel Museum collections. Open only to photographers based in the Chicago area able to deliver work in person. Exhibition July 2–26, 2026 at Perspective Gallery, Evanston, IL. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: $35 / 5 images. Prize: $200 Juror's Award + $150 + $100.

item.title: see-zeen Issue 20 Open Call
item.description: Independent online magazine curating contemporary photography by international emerging artists, based in NYC and Berlin. Open theme — any style, genre, or approach (portraiture, landscape, documentary, fashion, abstraction, experimental, conceptual, hybrid). Selected work published on website and social media; unpublished submissions still considered for Instagram. Submit a project statement (max 300 words), work description (max 100 words), bio with contact, and website/Instagram links. — Deadline: May 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photo Trouvée Magazine Issue 20 — Print Call
item.description: Print Issue 20 open call for artists who work with or are inspired by vintage found or family photographs. Any media accepted. Selected artists receive a designated page spread with artist statement, complimentary digital issue, 15% discount code for the print magazine, plus website, newsletter, and social media listings reaching 23.2K+ people. No theme. International submissions welcome. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $40 if selected. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Remnants — Spring 2026 Online Exhibition · Analog Forever Magazine
item.description: Online group exhibition exploring photography's relationship to loss and absence — family members, homes, ways of life, places, objects, and memories. Curated by Michael Behlen, founder of Analog Forever Magazine. Open to photographers working with film and analog processes. Optional but encouraged: a paragraph on what the subject means to you and why. Exhibition launches online May 29, 2026. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: The House & Garden Show · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description: Online exhibition exploring shelter and nature through intimate interiors, domestic moments, wild backyards, and cultivated landscapes. Literal, abstract, or imaginary interpretations welcome. Part of Blue Sky Gallery's 50th anniversary celebration featuring 12 monthly themed online exhibitions. No membership required. Juried by a special committee. Virtual exhibition launches June 4, 2026. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Pamplemousse Magazine Issue 13
item.description: Issue 13 of Pamplemousse Magazine, an independent contemporary film photography print magazine based in San Francisco. This call invites artists to respond to provided curated vernacular photographs — exploring the intersection of snapshot and fine art photography. Only original film photography (35mm, 120, large format, polaroid, or alt-process) created in response to one of the provided found photos is accepted. A project statement of 100–300 words is required. Files named FIRSTNAME_LASTNAME_01. — Deadline: May 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: The Life of Color · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis exploring how color operates as signal — amplifying, unifying, or destabilizing what is seen. Photographers encouraged to use hue, saturation, and value deliberately to construct meaning. Up to 38 photographs selected. Awards include Directors' Choice (free entry to two future calls) and five honorable mentions. Members and artists experiencing financial hardship receive discounted or free entries. Exhibition June 20 – July 11, 2026. — Deadline: May 17, 2026. Fee: $35 for 5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: imagined · A Smith Gallery
item.description: Online juried exhibition exploring the imaginative — visionary, poetic, fanciful, dreamlike, fictional. Juror Susan Burnstine, an award-winning fine art photographer known for creating homemade cameras and lenses. Up to 47 images selected. Awards: Juror's Award (solo online exhibition, hardbound book, blog feature), Director's Award (hardbound book and blog feature), Visitor's Award ($100 for most Instagram likes). Exhibition June 19 – July 30, 2026. Photographers submitting 13+ images receive a complimentary 30-minute portfolio review. — Deadline: May 25, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ABANDONED Photography Exhibit · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Exploring traces of human presence and absence — forgotten structures, deserted landscapes, personal relics, and emotional remnants. 26 selected images exhibited at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe, NM, July 3–31, 2026. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Luster paper and 24×24 black museum-quality framing. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. — Deadline: May 22, 2026. Fee: $40–$45. Prize: Exhibition + free printing & framing.

item.title: 10th Singapore International Photography Festival 2026 Open Call
item.description: 10th biennial SIPF Open Call for image-makers and photographers worldwide, with no theme. Two categories: Portfolio (cohesive body of work in images and/or video) and Photobook (both published and dummy books, which must be production-ready in physical form). Shortlisted submissions presented in the SIPF Open Call Showcase at the 10th biennale edition of SIPF in Singapore, mid-October to end-November 2026. Three SGD $2,000 cash prizes awarded: Best Portfolio, Best Published Photobook, Best Dummy Photobook. Shortlisted artists receive exposure to SIPF's network, discounted portfolio reviews and masterclasses, complimentary festival admission, and opportunities to participate in artist tours, talks, and workshops. Organised by DECK Photography Art Centre, a registered Charity in Singapore supported by the National Arts Council. Submission fee: USD $30 for Photobook, USD $45 for Portfolio. — Deadline: May 17, 2026. Fee: $30–$45. Prize: 3× SGD $2,000.

item.title: Filter Space 2026/27 Call for Exhibition Proposals · Filter Photo
item.description: Annual open call for exhibition proposals at Filter Space, Filter Photo's Chicago gallery. Selected artists, curators, and collectives receive a 4–6 week exhibition in 2027–2028, at least one reception, an event hosting opportunity (artist talk, panel, or workshop), printed marketing materials and press releases, and a W.A.G.E. Standards-based stipend ($1,250 for solo shows; $625/artist for two-person; $315/artist for groups of 3–5). Proposals should relate to photography, photographic materials, or lens-based artwork, including moving-image pieces, installations, and performances connected to photography. Submit an artist or curatorial statement (500 words max), bio and CV for all participants, 10–12 sample images (JPEG, 1000 px longest side), and links to video/multimedia (max 5 minutes). Review in July 2026; announcement in August 2026. — Deadline: June 17, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: 4–6 week exhibition + W.A.G.E. stipend.

item.title: Slow Exposures 2026 — Main Exhibition
item.description: Annual juried exhibition celebrating photography of the contemporary American South. Work must be taken in one of 16 Southern states: Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and West Virginia. Selected photographs shown first at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in downtown Concord, GA, then move to the Cochran Gallery in LaGrange, GA. 30% commission on sales. Festival weekend September 18–20, 2026 in Zebulon, Georgia. Submit up to 6 images via Formsite. 23rd edition. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: $50 for 6 images. Prize: Exhibition in rural Georgia.

item.title: Studio Museum in Harlem Artist-in-Residence 2026–2027
item.description: Eleven-month residency (November 2, 2026 – October 3, 2027) for three artists of African and Afro-Latinx descent working in any media, including photography. Residents receive a $50,000 stipend paid biweekly, 24-hour access to a private studio and shared spaces within the museum, institutional guidance, professional development, research support, and regular studio visits with the curatorial team. Culminating exhibition and publication at Studio Museum June–September 2027. Open to artists 18+ at all career stages (geared toward emerging practitioners). Local, national, and international artists eligible. Submit CV, 5–10 images or videos of work, and artist statement. Letters of recommendation encouraged but not required. — Deadline: May 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $50,000 stipend + studio.

item.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Impermanence
item.description: New themed issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. This call, guest curated by Benjamin Osborne, explores the theme Impermanence — the fleeting, the ephemeral, shadows and transient forms that open doors to imagination. Issue 03 featuring 11 artists including Alena Solomonova, Nova Doria, and Mari Saxon was just released. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px) with a project description. Upload work to Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files Name_Series_Title_01. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers. — Deadline: May 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Ucross Foundation Spring 2027 Residency
item.description: 2–6 week residency on a 20,000-acre ranch in northern Wyoming. Private studio, living quarters, chef-prepared meals Monday–Friday, weekly housekeeping, and a stipend. Application portal opens May 1 and closes July 15, 2026 for the Spring 2027 session (February – early June 2027). Approximately 115 artists hosted annually, with up to 10 in residence at any time. Open to visual artists (including photographers), writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary and performance artists, and collaborative teams. Both emerging and established artists of professional standing are welcome. Notification approximately 16 weeks after the deadline. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Residency + stipend.

item.title: Create! Magazine Issue #58 — In Full Color
item.description: Open call for Issue No. 58, 'In Full Color.' Artists respond to the concept of color in any artistic interpretation — hue, cultural expression, emotion, or otherwise. Photography welcomed alongside painting, sculpture, installation, and other media. Selected artists receive a four-page professional spread in the print and digital editions of the fall 2026 issue, plus social media features and a complimentary digital issue. Juried by Liz Lidgett (art advisor and gallery owner, Des Moines, Iowa). Submit up to 10 works (cohesive bodies or series encouraged). Open to all artists worldwide, no formal education or gallery representation required. No AI-generated work. — Deadline: May 30, 2026. Fee: $35 / 3 images. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Baxter St 2026–2027 Guest Curatorial Open Call
item.description: Annual open call for emerging independent curators and artist-curators to propose exhibitions at Baxter St at the Camera Club of New York. Three guest-curated shows selected per year for 2026–2027 season. Projects should contribute to contemporary lens-based arts dialogue and demonstrate innovative curatorial approaches, with preference for artists not yet represented by New York galleries. Maximum two artists per proposal; curator cannot be an exhibiting artist. Curator fee plus artist fees and full production budget provided. Curators must be located in the tri-state area (NY, NJ, CT) at the time of exhibition. Cannot have exhibited at Baxter St in the previous two years. Submit overview, 300-word concept statement, up to 8 images and up to 2 videos (max 3 min each). — Deadline: May 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Curator and artist fees + production budget.

item.title: Fresh Eyes x Hungry Eye vol. 2
item.description: Second Fresh Eyes x Hungry Eye collaboration, an international open call for emerging photographers powered by Amsterdam-based GUP Magazine. Selected artists receive minimum 4 pages in a softcover publication with international distribution to galleries, curators, agencies, and media, plus promotion through GUP and Fresh Eyes channels. One image from each selected artist is displayed in a group exhibition at Hungry Eye Fair, Amsterdam (September 2026), with two free entry tickets. Selected photographers also receive three copies of the publication and portfolio review opportunities. Three 'Exceptional Talent Award' winners receive free publication inclusion. Jury of GUP editors, gallerists and photographers. Free to apply; selected participants pay €350 (excluding VAT and shipping). Open worldwide to emerging photographers. — Deadline: May 20, 2026. Fee: Free (€350 participation fee if selected). Prize: Publication + exhibition at Hungry Eye Fair.

item.title: Copenhagen Photo Festival 2026 Open Exhibition
item.description: Annual open exhibition at Copenhagen Photo Festival 2026 on the theme 'Forestil dig...?' (Imagine if...?). 50 selected works printed, framed, and exhibited at the Royal Theatre (Det Kongelige Teater) from 11–17 June 2026. Non-selected submissions shown digitally during the festival (11–21 June 2026). Submit one square (1:1) JPG at 300 dpi, printable at 30×30 cm. Prizes: 4,000 DKK / 2,000 DKK / 1,000 DKK CEWE printing vouchers. Selected photographers get free festival access and reception invitation. Open internationally to photographers 18+. — Deadline: May 5, 2026. Fee: 35 DKK. Prize: 4,000 / 2,000 / 1,000 DKK voucher + Royal Theatre exhibition.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Local Landscapes
item.description: Submit up to 5 local landscape images with captions for publication in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK), issue OP 329. Winner receives Sunski Ferrata sunglasses (RRP £149.95). JPG at 300ppi. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Illuminations Grant 2026 · Queer|Art
item.description: Annual grant supporting Black trans women and trans femmes working in visual art. One winner receives $10,000; four finalists each receive $1,250. Winners also receive professional development resources and studio visits with rotating panel judges. Developed in partnership with photographer Mariette Pathy Allen, activist Aaryn Lang, and artist Serena Jara. Accepted media include photography, drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, and fiber arts. Open to self-identified Black trans women and trans femmes in early-career visual-art practice, based in the United States. Apply via SlideRoom with up to 12 work samples, two short statements on artistic practice, CV, and two professional references. — Deadline: July 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 + 4 × $1,250.

item.title: Print Swap Inaugural Exhibition
item.description: Inaugural open call from Print Swap, a new iOS app founded by London photographer Sam Faulkner for direct print-for-print exchanges between photographers. 50 selected images are printed and exhibited at The Print Space in London, opening May 7, 2026. Selected photographers receive permanent Founding Artists status in the app. All printing and exhibition costs are covered. Submissions made via the Print Swap iOS app. Open to photographers worldwide. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Al & Mickey Quinlan Artist Residency 2026 · Miller Art Museum
item.description: Eight-week residency at the Dome House — a twin-lobed concrete structure built into sand dunes on Lake Michigan adjacent to Whitefish Dunes State Park on Wisconsin's Door Peninsula. Open to one artist residing in the Midwest US (Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota) working in drawing, painting, printmaking, photography or related fine-art mediums. 2026 residency runs August 2 – September 27. Semi-private loft living quarters and adjacent studio/workspace provided, fully furnished. Resident must provide a minimum of 5 hours/week of educational outreach (workshops, artist talks, demonstrations). Partnership between the Quinlan family and the Miller Art Museum. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 8-week residency + $500 stipend + housing.

item.title: From Your Archive · L.A. Photo Curator
item.description: Open call juried by Laurie Freitag, founder of L.A. Photo Curator, inviting photographers to submit work from their existing archives — images that feel clear, resolved, and hold over time, across all photographic styles. First place receives a solo online exhibition, a featured Q&A article, and homepage feature for one month. All selected photographers appear in a group online exhibition with artist statement and bio, with consideration for Top 40 Images of the Year and Photographer of the Year. 5% of entry fees donated to No Kid Hungry; additional 5% to the winner's chosen charity. AI-generated work not accepted. Submit 3 or 6 images (not 4 or 5). Limited fee waivers available on request. Open worldwide. — Deadline: May 3, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Solo online exhibition + feature.

item.title: Tasweer 2026 Project Award
item.description: Annual grant from Tasweer, Qatar's leading photo festival organised by Qatar Museums. Open to photographers aged 18+ currently residing in the Western Asia and North Africa (WANA) region — Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Turkey, UAE, and Yemen. The award provides 30,000 QAR (~$8,200) per awardee to support the initiation, development, or completion of a photographic project. Winners receive opportunities to exhibit at Tasweer Photo Festival Qatar and participate in public and digital programming. Applicants may apply simultaneously to the Single Image Award. Submit one PDF file containing 20 images with titles and captions. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 30,000 QAR (~$8,200).

item.title: Tasweer 2026 Single Image Award
item.description: Annual single-image competition from Tasweer, Qatar's photo festival organised by Qatar Museums. Open to photographers aged 18+ currently residing in the Western Asia and North Africa (WANA) region. Each photographer submits one image representing their personal narrative and experience. Winners receive 2,000 QAR per awardee, with selected images showcased in an online exhibition and featured as part of Tasweer Photo Festival Qatar's public and digital programme. Submit one JPEG or TIFF, 3000 pixels max on longest side, 3–8 MB. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2,000 QAR (~$550).

item.title: Recology San Francisco Artist-in-Residence Program 2027
item.description: Four-month Artist-in-Residence program at the Recology San Francisco Recycling and Transfer Center, where artists source materials from the Public Reuse and Recycling Area to make work from discarded items. Three sessions run February–May, June–September, and October–January, with six artists awarded residencies annually beginning February 2027. Residents receive a monthly stipend, 24/7 access to a dedicated on-site studio, and support from Recology's Sustainability Education Program. Artists interact with visiting school and adult groups throughout their residency and exhibit at the end. Open to emerging, mid-career, and established artists in all disciplines including photography, new media, video, painting, performance, sculpture, and installation. Applicants must currently live within a one-hour drive of the San Francisco Transfer Station (401 Tunnel Ave) — no housing provided. A mandatory on-site tour is required before applying. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Stipend.

item.title: Eco-Process Artist Residency 2026 · grunt gallery
item.description: One-month summer residency at Blue Cabin Floating Artist Residency in Metro Vancouver (August 2026) for emerging lens-based artists. Program focuses on eco-processing and alternative photographic techniques such as phytogram, lumen printing, cyanotype, and other sustainable photographic processes. Up to 3 mentorship sessions with interdisciplinary artist Morgan Sears-Williams. Blue Cabin is situated on the traditional territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh Nations. Priority given to LGBTQ+ 2S emerging artists with some photo/lens-based experience. Open to emerging artists in Metro Vancouver and Indigenous territories/reserves connected to the region. Produced by grunt gallery in collaboration with Blue Cabin Cooperative. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,500.

item.title: 2026 National Juried Photography Exhibition
item.description: Juried photography exhibition at the Academy Center of the Arts in Lynchburg, Virginia. Open to U.S. residents aged 18+. Photographs must be original work completed after January 1, 2021, not previously exhibited in a Lynchburg juried photography show. Juror Kiera Hight, photographer and filmmaker from Asheville, NC, selects work after installation. Exhibition runs September 4–25, 2026 with an opening reception on September 4. Digital submissions accepted via email or flash drive; JPEG, 300 DPI, minimum 4×6". — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $1,000 Best in Show.

item.title: Abbott Watts Photography Residency — Fall 2026 · Monson Arts
item.description: Dedicated photography residency at Monson Arts in Maine, with access to the photography studio and darkroom of Todd Watts in nearby Blanchard — adjacent to the former home of Berenice Abbott. Darkroom accommodates silver gelatin printing up to 40"×50" from 35mm to 8×10 negatives, plus alternative analog processes. Digital studio with PC workstations, 34" monitors, Adobe Creative Cloud, and a 44" Epson printer. Residents receive a private bedroom in shared housing in Monson, all meals, and a stipend ($250 for 2-week, $500 for 4-week). Fall 2026 sessions: September 14–24 (2-week) and October 28 – November 19 (4-week). Residents must supply their own materials and have a car (8-minute drive to studio). Open to photographers at any career stage worldwide. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Check site. Prize: Residency + stipend.

item.title: Peyton Evans Artist Residency (PEAR) 2026–2027 · The Studios of Key West
item.description: One-month residency program on Key West, Florida. Photographers apply under Media Arts. Residencies run the 2nd day of the month to the last day, between October 2026 and August 2027. Residents receive accommodation at the PEAR House (live/work space), a bike to get around the island, and access to shared kitchen facilities. No residency fee once accepted; artists cover their own travel, living expenses, and materials. Founded in 2006, The Studios has hosted hundreds of writers and artists; selection committees are comprised of working artists and professionals across Visual Arts, Literary Arts, Media Arts, Musical Arts, and Performing Arts. Apply via SlideRoom. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Check site. Prize: One-month live/work residency.

item.title: The Colour Library: Yellow — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
item.description: Open call for The Colour Library: Yellow, part of Shutter Hub's curated series exploring the emotional, symbolic, and visual power of individual colours. This edition is dedicated to yellow — bold and joyful, energetic and optimistic, but also capable of signalling caution, unease, or something hauntingly strange. Welcomes all approaches from bold monochromes to subtle glows, conceptual or documentary. Selected photographers featured in a professionally produced photobook held in international collections including the British Library and V&A. 100 images will be selected. Featured photographers receive promotion and a dedicated page on the Shutter Hub website. Pay-what-you-can entry with £15 minimum. Free submissions on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide. — Deadline: July 16, 2026. Fee: £15+. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: Lucie Foundation Scholarship Program 2026
item.description: Annual program offering four cash grants across two categories (Fine Art and Photojournalism/Documentary), each split between Professional and Emerging photographers. Prizes: Fine Art Professional $3,000 + Fine Art Emerging $1,000 + Photojournalism/Documentary Professional $3,000 + Photojournalism/Documentary Emerging $1,000 plus a Sony camera and lens. Winners featured in a group exhibition that travels to House of Lucie Galleries worldwide (Los Angeles, Athens, Budapest, Ostuni, Samui). 'Professional' means earning majority of income from photography; 'Emerging' means enrolled students, photographers in their first five years, or those who don't earn majority from photography. Early bird discounts: 20% off until April 23, 10% off until April 30. Applicants submit a project proposal (1,500 characters max), one-page bio/CV, and 20 digital images. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18+. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $15–25. Prize: $8,000.

item.title: PLACE/MEMORY — CONTACT Photography Festival · Northern Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Open call photography exhibition at Northern Contemporary Gallery in Toronto, presented as part of the 2026 CONTACT Photography Festival — Canada's largest photography festival. Photographers are invited to submit work that represents their current practice through the medium of photography, responding to the theme PLACE/MEMORY. Physical group exhibition runs May 21 – June 2, 2026, with an opening reception on May 21, 6–9pm. One submission per artist via the official Google form. Work drop-off May 19; pick-up June 3. Part of the CONSTELLATION program curated by Su-Ying Lee and Emilie Croning. — Deadline: May 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Art-in-Ed Workspace Residency 2026
item.description: 6–7 week workspace residency combining teaching with personal studio practice at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Artists teach intaglio, silkscreen, or hand papermaking to local public school students — fourth and/or eighth graders three days/week for three weeks in Spring (elementary) or high school students one day/week for 4 weeks in Fall (plus school visits). Outside of teaching, artists work independently in any WSW studio including darkroom photography. Residency includes $175/day per teaching day plus $525 for lesson planning, free housing, and 24/7 studio access. Artist covers travel and materials. Fall 2026 cohort teaches high school; Spring 2027 cohort teaches elementary. Applications open February 15; notification in July. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $175/day + $525 lesson planning.

item.title: Nordic Artists' Centre Dale 2027 Residency
item.description: Two-to-four-month residency in 2027 at NKD, a non-profit centre funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality in the village of Dale, Fjaler on Norway's west coast. Established 1998. Residents receive a monthly grant of NOK 11,000, up to NOK 5,000 in travel reimbursement, and free accommodation in a private residence house plus a 50m² studio with 6-metre ceilings and north-lit panorama windows. Open to professional visual artists, designers, and architects (photographers welcome). Not available to students or practitioners in music, writing, dance, or theatre. Residents give a presentation and participate in an open studio day. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: NOK 11,000/month.

item.title: Cavendish Arts Science Fellowship 2026–27
item.description: Annual fellowship in partnership with Girton College, Cambridge, supporting artists to engage with physicists and others at the Cavendish Laboratory. Runs October 2026 – October 2027 with a Cambridge residency of 6–12 months (can be split across visits). Includes £10,000 stipend, £10,000 production budget, up to £3,000 travel support, rent-free accommodation and meals at Girton College, and a studio/creative workspace plus flexible working spaces at the Cavendish Laboratory. Open internationally to artists of any medium or nationality — no prior science experience required. Must be 18+ and out of full-time education by October 2026. Joint applications accepted. — Deadline: May 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £23,000.

item.title: Chester Photo Festival 2026 — Making Voices Heard
item.description: Second edition of the annual Chester Photo Festival, running 16–29 October 2026 across University of Chester, Picturehouse, churches, and a museum. Theme: Making Voices Heard — exploring photography through myths, feelings, memories, and personal narratives. Free entry of up to 5 works; selection fees only apply if chosen (£45/work early deadline 15 May, £60/work late deadline 15 June, covering printing and standard framing). Open to photographers of all experience levels internationally. Accepts photography, moving image (online link + still), and artist books (PDF). Selected works included in the exhibition book and displayed across Chester venues. Late entries close when 300 works are selected. Organised by academics and researchers including Dr Alexandru Modoi and Professor Erik Knudsen. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: Free entry; £45–£60 per selected work. Prize: Exhibition + book publication.

item.title: BEERS London Group Exhibition 2026
item.description: Open call for a group exhibition of approximately 12 artists at BEERS London, a contemporary gallery in the heart of the City. All artistic media welcome including photography. Selected artists consigned for exhibition period plus up to three months, with 50/50 commission split on sales. Gallery actively promotes selected work to collectors. No guaranteed representation or sales. Open worldwide. Exhibition runs August–September 2026. Selected artists notified approximately four months before opening. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: £10. Prize: Group exhibition at BEERS London.
